newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: ING RATES SLOVAK HYDRO-CONSTRUCTION EUROBOND BUY.
newsitem.headline: ING RATES SLOVAK HYDRO-CONSTRUCTION EUROBOND BUY.

text.p: ING Barings, in an investor report, said it considers Eurobonds issued by Slovak state-owned hydro-construction firm Vodohospodarska Vystavba a.s. (VVB) to be undervalued and recommends them as a buy.
"We view the bond as slightly undervalued and believe that the spread will tighten in the near to mid term given the guarantor's strong fundamentals," the report said.
The bond, issued on December 5 at 99.691 (115 basis points over U.S treasuries), was oversubscribed on the primary auction due to its attractive price.

Dusan Meszaros, a debt analysts of ING Barings Bratislava, told Reuters that the paper was now trading at 95 to 105 basis points over U.S treasuries and that he expected it to climb to around 85 points within one month.
The bond pays a fixed annual coupon of 7.25 percent.
The issue is fully guaranteed by the state and carries Slovakia's sovereign debt rating -- Standard & Poor's BBB minus long-term foreign currency denominated debt rating and Moody's Baa3 rating.

"In light of the strategic importance of VVB's activities and strong governmental support, we strongly recommend (buying) the issue," ING said. The government's loan guarantees for VVB total 12.4 billion crowns ($400 million).
VVB is involved in major state-funded or guaranteed investment programmes of construction of hydro-electric power plants, water reservoirs and water management facilities.
The most important of such projects has been the construction of the controversial dam and the hydro power plant on the river Danube.
The company is included in the government list of the strategic firms which are excluded from privatisation and which are protected by law against going bankrupt.
The $200 million Eurobond issue, the first such paper of the Slovak commercial entity, was the second tranche of the VVB's $500 million loan facility managed by JP Morgan.
The company drew the first $200 million in December 1995. The final $100 million tranche of the credit is expected to be signed for later this year.
